profilePeriod: Chancellorship, December 2021–May 2025, including the final election programme.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

sources.title: Scholz inaugural Bundesrat speech
sources.evidence: Praised shared federal/Länder competencies, regional diversity, Bundesrat compromises and common national pandemic standards; supported general vaccine obligation.

sources.title: Bundestag confidence vote
sources.evidence: Scholz submitted to parliamentary confidence vote after coalition collapse, opening constitutional route to early elections.

sources.title: Scholz statement on security
sources.evidence: Argued security underpins liberty, democracy and rule of law; backed removal of serious foreign criminals and firm security action while maintaining international-law commitments.

sources.title: Health ministry: controlled adult cannabis
sources.evidence: Government cannabis reform allowed regulated adult possession and cultivation with youth and health protections, not unlimited legalization of all drugs.

sources.title: Modern citizenship law
sources.evidence: Scholz welcomed immigrants as part of Germany; dual citizenship, shorter residence qualification, German-language and constitutional loyalty criteria, rejection of racism and antisemitism.

sources.title: AP: Scholz challenger and border rules
sources.evidence: Scholz promised to continue reducing irregular migration and increasing deportations after the Aschaffenburg knife attack.

sources.title: Scholz Zeitenwende speech
sources.evidence: Promised €100 billion military fund and NATO commitments, arms for Ukraine, sanctions on Russia and allied deployments. Rejected aggression; kept dialogue open and emphasized EU/international order.

sources.title: AP: 2025 election programmes
sources.evidence: SPD platform supported €15 wage and reform of borrowing rules for investment; government argued its border measures were reducing irregular migration.

sources.title: ARD: 2025 party programmes
sources.evidence: SPD retained Scholz refusal to supply Taurus missiles to Ukraine. Used only SPD section, not positions of other parties.

sources.title: Uniper stabilization agreement
sources.evidence: Federal rescue proposed 99 percent ownership and KfW credit for Uniper to safeguard energy supply; this was a crisis intervention, not universal collectivization.

sources.title: Scholz IHK Cologne speech
sources.evidence: Advocated Deutschlandfonds involving public and private capital for grids, technology and housing and a limited borrowing-rule opening for renewal and security.

sources.title: Reuters: talks on Chinese EVs
sources.evidence: Scholz opposed shutting out foreign competition and urged continued negotiation with China instead of trade restrictions.

sources.title: AP: EU votes on EV tariffs
sources.evidence: Germany opposed EU Chinese electric-vehicle tariffs, corroborating trade openness despite domestic industry support.

sources.title: Scholz Protestant Church reception
sources.evidence: Affirmed separation of state and church while praising churches for community, refugee help and deliberation. Distinguished humanitarian asylum from unlimited immigration.

sources.title: Federal civic education agency: self-determination law
sources.evidence: Coalition-supported law enabled simpler gender-entry changes from November 2024, with safeguards for minors. Medical treatment rules remained separate.

sources.title: SPD Women on election programme
sources.evidence: Programme endorsed gender equality and removal of abortion section 218 from criminal law. Party self-description, cross-checked with parliamentary reform proposal.

sources.title: Bundestag proposal on section 218
sources.evidence: Proposed early abortion no longer unlawful through twelve weeks; later procedures would retain restrictions with medical exceptions.

sources.title: Scholz Digital Summit speech
sources.evidence: Promoted AI, quantum computing, fusion, aerospace, biotechnology and environmental technology with public/private investment and productivity gains.

sources.title: Deutschlandfunk interview: no nuclear return
sources.evidence: Scholz ruled out reviving conventional nuclear power in Germany; his industrial technological optimism does not imply embracing every technology.

sources.title: Hoffmann und Campe: Hoffnungsland
sources.evidence: Publisher search record identifies Olaf Scholz and publication on 17 March 2017; direct open failed during this audit.

sources.title: EconBiz library catalogue: Hoffnungsland
sources.evidence: Catalogue search record confirms author Olaf Scholz, full German title and 2017 publication; political contents concern migration and Germany. Live site later returned bot interstitial.

sources.title: Tagesspiegel: Scholz on future German society
sources.evidence: Contemporaneous independent book report identifies Hoffnungsland: Eine neue deutsche Wirklichkeit as his first book, about migration, Europe, right populism and open society.

facts: 2022 Bundesrat address explicitly defended shared federal authority and regional solutions.
National pandemic standards and equal living conditions remained goals.
estrutura.tension: Cooperative federalism is not unilateral secession, local veto of all national rules or fiscal isolation.

facts: 2024 confidence procedure returned political authority to Parliament and voters.
representacao.tension: Representative constitutional democracy does not imply replacing elected representatives with sortition or permanent assemblies.

facts: 2024 security speech supported firm lawful policing and deportation of dangerous offenders.
2022 vaccine obligation advocacy coexisted with 2024 regulated cannabis reform.
poder.tension: Civil rights within rule of law coexist with public-health mandates and security powers; do not treat economic statism as police authoritarianism.

facts: 2024 citizenship reform embraced dual identity and civic/language integration.
January 2025 position stressed reduction of irregular migration and deportations.
imigracao.tension: Not open borders, but immigration restrictions concern legal status, capacity and criminal conduct, not ethnic or cultural purity.

facts: 2022 Zeitenwende funded rearmament and NATO deterrence.
2025 SPD campaign retained refusal of Taurus while supporting Ukraine.
diplomacia.tension: Armed deterrence and diplomacy together; neither military abolition nor preventive war.

facts: 2022 backed NATO deployments, sanctions and arms for Ukraine within alliances.
Defended UN principles and rejected spheres of influence.
intervencao.tension: Restraint against direct Russian war differs from neutrality, isolation or opposition to sanctions.

facts: 2022 Uniper crisis rescue used near-total state ownership and public-bank finance.
2025 investment fund invited private capital alongside government.
economia.tension: Mixed social-market economy with essential public services, not expropriation of all private production.

facts: 2025 platform backed higher statutory wages and investment-friendly debt reform.
Public coordination in energy, housing and technology included private business.
controle.tension: Strong regulation and strategic investment do not imply a fully planned economy or abolition of monetary institutions.

facts: October 2024 opposed blocking Chinese competition and Germany voted against EV tariffs.
Strategic energy and industrial resilience remained priorities.
comercio.tension: Sectoral resilience and subsidies coexist with export-oriented free trade; no autarky or blanket tariff programme.

facts: 2023 EKD speech defended church/state separation while welcoming church community and humanitarian work.
religiao.tension: Secular public authority without hostility to believers, religious education or voluntary traditions.

facts: 2024 coalition backed gender self-determination.
2025 campaign supported equality and early abortion decriminalization.
moral.tension: Private pluralism and equal rights remain bounded by consent and protection of minors; Brazilian racial quotas require contextual inference.

facts: October 2024 championed AI, biotech, fusion, aerospace and industrial productivity.
September 2023 rejected a German conventional nuclear restart.
tecnologia.tension: Pro-innovation does not settle germline enhancement, brain implants or every environmental tradeoff; therapeutic benefit differs from designer children.

uncertainties: Historical chancellorship period preserved explicitly; later personal positions and successor policies are not attributed to Scholz. Research accessed on 2026-10-01.
Brazil-specific examples interpreted by transferable political principle rather than invented direct statements about Brazil.
No direct statements verified on all speculative biotechnology, polyamory, racial-quota or euthanasia questions; answers are reasoned inferences, not quotations.
Government and party sources establish declared positions, not proof of policy success. Coalition law is weaker evidence of personal intensity than direct speeches.

German title verified; targeted searches for Portuguese/Brazilian and English editions found no verified translations. Original title retained. Publisher and library full pages were intermittently unavailable; contemporaneous independent review corroborates book.
